about.title: Folsom Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Folsom sits on the east edge of Sacramento County, and much of its daily driving happens on a handful of busy surface streets rather than a freeway. In 2025, the city recorded 80 injury collisions, with 113 people hurt and 6 traffic deaths. Public collision records show E Bidwell Street, Iron Point Road, Blue Ravine Road, and Riley Street carry the highest counts, and reports cluster on Wednesdays between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters are heading home. If one of those crashes involved you, the days that follow can feel scattered: a damaged car, doctor visits, and calls from an adjuster asking for a recorded statement. You are not required to give one. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match people injured in Folsom with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California allows two years to file most claims, but as little as six months when a public agency is involved, so preserving photos, records, and witness names early makes a real difference.

items.title: Deadlines That Move Faster Than You Expect
items.desc: California gives most crash victims two years to file, but a claim against a city, county, or state agency can require notice in just six months. An attorney can sort out which clock applies to your Folsom collision before it runs out.

items.title: Fault Is Shared, Not All-or-Nothing
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly responsible, with your share reduced by your percentage of blame. That is one reason not to accept an adjuster's early version of what happened.

items.title: No Fee Unless There Is a Recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life in ordinary car accident cases. Our connection service costs you nothing.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not obligated to provide a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and it is usually wise to hold off until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use your words to shift a larger share of fault onto you under California's comparative fault rules. Instead, gather photos, the police report number, and witness contact information, and let a lawyer handle communications.

items.question: I was hit near Iron Point Road during the evening commute. Does the location matter to my claim?
items.answer: It can. Many of Folsom's reported collisions occur on corridors like Iron Point Road and E Bidwell Street, often during the Wednesday 5 to 7 p.m. peak, which means nearby businesses or traffic cameras may have captured footage. That video is frequently overwritten within days, so requesting it quickly is one of the first steps an attorney will take. The location also matters if a road condition or signal issue points toward a government entity, which triggers a much shorter filing window.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Folsom?
items.answer: For most car accident injury claims in California, the statute of limitations is two years from the date of the crash. If a public agency such as the City of Folsom, Sacramento County, or a state department may share responsibility, you generally must file a government claim within six months. Because missing either deadline can end your case, it is best to speak with an attorney early rather than waiting on the insurance process.
